text:
marie: Hey folks, new hire here. Trying to run `./bin/migrate` locally but I get:

`psql: could not connect to server: No such file or directory
	Is the server running locally and accepting connections on Unix domain socket "/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432"?`

I do have the dev compose up and `docker ps` shows `0.0.0.0:5442->5432/tcp`. My compose snippet:
```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:15
    ports:
      - "5442:5432"
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=devpass
```

owen: Welcome! libpq (psql etc.) prefers unix sockets when PGHOST is unset. If you run the app on the host and want TCP to the container, set `PGHOST=localhost` or run `psql -h localhost -p 5442`.

marie: Oh interesting. I was following the README which just ran `psql -U postgres` and assumed it would pick the published port.

infra-bot: infra-bot posted: "reminder: onboarding docs updated last month to mention PGHOST and socket vs tcp behavior"

lee: A couple more gotchas we've seen: 1) If you're on mac/Windows and using a corporate VPN (looking at you, AnyConnect), `host.docker.internal` can stop resolving or be routed oddly. If your app runs inside WSL, `host.docker.internal` is usually right; if on Windows host, `localhost` is often easier. 2) Some people try to mount the host postgres socket into a container to share it — messy and platform-dependent. Prefer TCP for dev.

sam: Quick reproducible suggestions: from host try `psql -h localhost -p 5442 -U postgres` and if that works, set `PGHOST=localhost` in your `.env.local`. Also check `echo $PGHOST` in the shell you run migrations from.

marie: `psql -h localhost -p 5442 -U postgres` worked! One more weirdness: earlier I tried `host.docker.internal:5442` and it failed when my VPN was on, but `localhost` worked. Good to know this is VPN-related.

owen: Yes — VPNs can hijack the docker DNS or routing. For the docs we call out: "If connections fail when using host.docker.internal while on VPN, try localhost or restart Docker Desktop." Also prefer named volumes for PG data to avoid permission issues across host OSes:
```yaml
volumes:
  pgdata:
services:
  db:
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

marie: Thanks — I'll update my local .env and open a tiny PR to add a note about sockets vs TCP + VPN gotchas. Appreciate the quick responses :tada:
